newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - April 17.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - April 17.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

Defiance Mills Ltd Chairman Tom O'Brien said late on Wednesday the board of Defiance would recommend shareholders reject Bunge Corp's revised takeover bid of A$1.95 a share. "The board of Defiance is still advising that the price is nowhere near high enough," O'Brien told Reuters. Earlier Bunge's announced it had raised its bid and secured acceptances from Defiance's major shareholder (43 percent), the O'Brien-family controlled Defiance Holdings Ltd.
MIM said on Thursday it expected to book a A$40 million abnormal profit from the restructuring of its Newlands-Collinsville Abbot Point coal project.

Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA) said on Thursday it had corrected a computer fault which processed 300,000 transactions twice on Tuesday evening. The fault had the effect of doubling the amount of every deposit or withdrawal or transfer for those 300,000 transactions.

U.S. tobacco executives are negotiating for the first time with state attorneys general on a possible settlement of massive litigation against the industry, several attorneys general said Wednesday. News about the settlement talks pushed tobacco stocks up sharply in the U.S.. Philip Morris rose $4.375 to close at $43.25 and Nabisco rose $3.25 to close at $33.50.

Canadian brewer Molson Breweries said on Wednesday that it has settled a dispute with U.S. beermaker Adolph Coors Co in their battle over Molson's licensing rights to Coors' top-selling beers in Canada. Under the agreement, Molson paid Coors C$100 million and will take a C$32.5 million after-tax charge against fiscal 1997 earnings. Molson also agreed to form a new partnership with Coors and Foster's Brewing Group to manage Coors brands in Canada. Foster's owns 40 pct of Molson.

Novus Petroleum Ltd, which has seen its stock trade at record levels this week, said on Wednesday that its part-owned Bukha gas field in Oman was offering the best returns of all the company's assets with returns on investment of over 20 percent plus. Novus shares have gained 27 cents to A$3.72 since Tuesday, when the company announced it was increasing its stake in the Bukha project to 40 percent from 10 percent.

Nomura International analyst Nick Woolf said on Wednesday night in London he repeated his "buy" rating on biotechnology group Cortecs International Ltd. Woolf estimated sales to grow by 33 percent in 1997 and by 155 percent in 1998. He was forecasting a re-rating of the stock after key trial data on treatment for osteoporosis, which has a potential market of $800 million. The Nomura report forced Cortecs' British shares up 45 pence to 282 pence in London on Wednesday.
Faulding's U.S. listed shares rose US$1/2 to 8 7/8 on talk of a broker upgrade.
